items.question: Why is UTF-8 safe encoding important for Base64?
items.answer: Standard browser btoa() throws an exception on Unicode characters like emojis and non-Latin scripts. Our tool uses TextEncoder and TextDecoder to ensure all Unicode characters are properly preserved.

items.question: What is URL-safe Base64 encoding?
items.answer: Standard Base64 uses "+" and "/" which have reserved meanings in URL parameters. URL-safe Base64 replaces "+" with "-" and "/" with "_", and omits trailing "=" padding characters.

items.question: Are my files uploaded to a remote server when encoding?
items.answer: Never. File reading and binary conversion occur entirely in your local browser memory using the FileReader and TypedArray APIs. Zero network requests are made.

items.question: What does the 76-character MIME wrap option do?
items.answer: The MIME standard (RFC 2045) specifies that Base64 email attachments and headers should be split into lines of at most 76 characters separated by CRLF line breaks.

items.question: How does the decoder handle missing padding or URL-safe characters?
items.answer: Our decoder automatically normalizes URL-safe characters and restores missing "=" padding before decoding, reporting clear syntax errors if invalid characters are detected.

items.question: What is a Data URI and how can I use it in HTML?
items.answer: A Data URI embeds raw file data directly into HTML or CSS (data:image/png;base64,...) eliminating extra HTTP requests for small logos or icons.

items.question: How does the encoder handle large binary files without freezing?
items.answer: Binary byte arrays are processed in discrete chunks of 3 bytes (yielding 4 ASCII characters), preventing memory stack overflows and browser thread locking.

items.question: Is decoded text guaranteed to match the original input byte-for-byte?
items.answer: Yes. Our Base64 engine undergoes automated roundtrip property tests proving that decode(encode(x)) strictly equals x for all arbitrary Unicode strings and byte buffers.
